key_insight: The paper shows that learned, hardware-aware figures of merit can predict quantum circuit execution quality much better than simple gate-count or depth metrics, and it introduces a weighted PST (wPST) that is more informative than standard PST.
engineering_relevance: For quantum compilers, these predictors can rank candidate circuits more reliably before execution, helping choose mappings that better respect device noise and coherence constraints.
method: Define and analyze desirable properties of an ideal figure of merit for circuit compilation
Propose wPST, which weights individual qubits instead of only evaluating the full returned state
Train machine-learning models using both circuit structure and hardware data, including a two-step predictor for non-transpiled circuits
evidence_signal: In simulations and experiments on quantum processors, the machine-learning-predicted FoMs improved correlation with true PST or wPST by more than 50% compared with commonly used metrics.
watch_item: The approach depends on hardware-specific data and an extra prediction step for gate overhead, so performance may vary when device characteristics drift or when circuits are far outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Comparing and learning figures of merit for quantum circuit compilation
